t2533.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Sulaymān b. al-Ashʿath al-Azdī al-Sijistānī, Abū Dāwūd, as trustworthy, a memorizer, compiler of the Sunan and other works, among the leading scholars of the eleventh generation; he died in 75.
as: ثقة حافظ مصنف السنن وغيرها من كبار العلماء
Trustworthy, a memorizer, compiler of the Sunan and other works, among the leading scholars.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
ويقال: إنه صنفه قديما وعرضه على أحمد بن حنبل فاستجاده واستحسنه
It is said he compiled it early and showed it to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who judged it good and approved it.
أبو بكر الخلال, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو داود الإمام المقدم في زمانه، رجل له يسبقه إلى معرفته بتخريج العلوم، وبصره بمواضعه أحد في زمانه، رجل ورع مقدم
Abū Dāwūd was the foremost imam of his time; no one in his time surpassed his knowledge of extracting the sciences and insight into them; a pious, eminent man.
إبراهيم الأصبهاني وأبو بكر بن صدقة, quoted by al-Mizzī
يرفعون من قدره ويذكرونه. بما لا يذكرون أحدا"في زمانه مثله
They exalted his standing and spoke of him as they spoke of no one else in his time.
أحمد بن محمد بن ياسين الهروي, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان أحد حفاظ الإسلام لحديث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلمه وعلله وسنده في أعلى درجة النسك والعفاف والصلاح والورع، من فرسان الحديث
He was one of Islam's memorisers of the Prophet's hadith, its knowledge, defects and chains, at the highest level of devotion, chastity, righteousness and piety; one of the champions of hadith.
محمد بن إسحاق الصاغاني، وإبراهيم بن إسحاق الحربي, quoted by al-Mizzī
لما صنف أبو داود كتاب"السنن"ألين لأبي داود الحديث كما الين لداود الحديد
When Abū Dāwūd compiled the Sunan, hadith was made pliant for him as iron was made pliant for David.
محمد بن مخلد, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان أبو داود يفي بمذاكرة مئة ألف حديث
Abū Dāwūd could hold his own in reviewing a hundred thousand hadith from memory.
موسى بن هارون الحافظ, quoted by al-Mizzī
خلق أبو داود في الدنيا للحديث، وفي الآخرة للجنة
Abū Dāwūd was created in this world for hadith and in the next for Paradise.
علان بن عبد الصمد, quoted by al-Mizzī
He was one of the champions of this field.
أبو داود أحد الأئمة الدنيا فقها وعلما وحفظا ونسكا وورعا وإتقانا، جمع وصنف وذب عن السنن
Abū Dāwūd was one of the world's imams in law, knowledge, memory, devotion, piety and precision; he collected, compiled and defended the Sunnah.
أبو عبد الله بن منده الحافظ, quoted by al-Mizzī
الذين اخرجوا وميزوا الثابت من المعلول، والخطأ من الصواب أربعة: البخاري، ومسلم، وبعد هما أبو داود السجستاني، وأبو عبد الرحمن النسائي
Those who published and separated the established from the defective and error from correct are four: al-Bukhārī, Muslim, then Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī and al-Nasāʾī.
الحاكم أبو عبد الله, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو داود إمام أهل الحديث في عصره بلا مدافعة
Abū Dāwūd was the undisputed imam of the hadith people in his era.

as: ثقة عابد إلا أنه لما كبر ساء حفظه وكتابه صحيح
Trustworthy and devout, but when he grew old his memory deteriorated; his book is sound.
ذكر ابن المبارك أبا بكر بن عياش فأثنى عليه
Ibn al-Mubārak spoke of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh and praised him.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Truthful, devoted to the Qurʾān and of good character.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
عثمان بن سعيد, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو بكر والحسن بنا عياش ليسا بذاك في الحديث، وهما من أهل الصدق والأمانة
Abū Bakr and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh do not rank highly in hadith, but they are truthful and trustworthy.
محمد بن عبد الله بن نمير, quoted by al-Mizzī
He is weak in reports from al-Aʿmash and others.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
هما في الحفظ سواء، غير إن أبا بكر أصح كتابا
He and Sharīk had equal retention, but Abū Bakr had the sounder book.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Bakr had better retention and was more reliable than ʿAbdallāh ibn Bishr al-Raqqī.
Ibn Ḥibbān included him in The Reliable Transmitters.
وهو في رواياته عن كل من روى عنه لا بأس به، وذلك إني لم أجد له حديثا منكرا إذا روى عنه ثقة إلا أن يروي عنه ضعيف
His reports from his teachers are acceptable. I found no objectionable reports when a reliable narrator transmitted from him, only when a weak narrator did.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Al-Ḥasan is reliable and Abū Bakr is reliable.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
His reports from Abū Isḥāq are close in quality to Abū al-Aḥwaṣ’s.
أبو حاتم الرازي, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما أقربهما، لا أبالي بايهما بدأت
Abū Bakr and Abū al-Aḥwaṣ were close, and I would not mind starting with either.
He was among those devoted to worship.
أعرف هذا الشيخ بهذه الصلاة منذ أربعين سنة
I have known this shaykh to pray like this for forty years.
وكان أبو بكر ثقة صدوقا عارفا بالحديث والعلم إلا أنه كثير الغلط
Abū Bakr was reliable, truthful and knowledgeable in hadith and learning, though he made many mistakes.

t8009.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū al-Jāriya al-ʿAbdī al-Baṣrī as unknown, of the tenth generation, cited by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī.

t8100.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Rafīʿ al-Makhdajī as acceptable, of the third generation, notes it is said his name is Rafīʿ, and lists Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah as citing him.

t8175.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Ṣāliḥ, client of Ḍubāʿah, weak in hadith, of the third generation; his name is Mīnā.

t8218.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū ʿAbd al-Dāʾim al-Hadādī, the Baṣran, named ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Kardūs, obscure, of the seventh generation.

t8283.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says Abū al-ʿAnbas al-Kūfī al-ʿAdawī, companion of Abū al-ʿAdbas, said to be named al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd, was acceptable, of the sixth generation.

t8427.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Hind al-Bajalī as a Syrian transmitter, acceptable in hadith, of the third generation. Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī transmit from him.
stu: Named next to each other in two or more indexed chains

t8492.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records the nephew of al-Ḥarith al-Aʿwar as unknown, of the sixth generation.
tch: Named next to each other in two or more indexed chains

t8625.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ṣafiyya bint ʿAṭiyya as unknown, also of the third generation.

t8650.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Fāṭima al-Zahrāʾ, daughter of the Messenger of God and Umm al-Ḥasan, chief of the women of this community; ʿAlī married her in the second year of the Hijra, and she died six months after the Prophet, just past twenty.
as: The chief of the women of this community.

t8791.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Usayd ibn Abī Usayd al-Barrād, from a woman among those who gave allegiance, whose name he could not find; she is a Companion with a hadith.

t937.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jaʿfar ibn Khālid ibn Sārah al-Makhzūmī, a Ḥijāzī, as trustworthy, of the seventh generation.
